speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Health with regard to the bivalent COVID-19 vaccines (a) when will the vaccines be made available; (b) how different is this booster vaccine from the original Moderna and Pfizer booster in terms of efficacy; and (c) when should a person who has recovered from COVID-19 take this vaccine.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A couple of the questions have been overtaken by events.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are planning to invite those aged between 18 and 49 for vaccination later in the year as we secure more supplies.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If you are infected, wait three months and you can take the bivalent vaccine, if you are eligible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Leon Perera had asked about reopening vaccination centres at community clubs and community centres.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Vaccination Centres (VCs) and Joint Testing and Vaccination Centres (JTVCs) are chosen based on their proximity to high population density areas, good accessibility and availability of the venue to support vaccination operations over a sustained period of time.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But as demand changes, we will continue to review the adequacy of this network.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Residents aged 50 and above who have already taken their second booster are not sure if they can take the bivalent vaccine and when to take it.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For those aged 80 and above, many took it in April, that is, more than five months but less than a year after the second booster.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For those aged 50 to 79, many took it in June, that is, less than five months of their second booster shot.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is a very common question we face on the ground.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I meet so many people that I have to repeatedly answer this question.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, for our residents who are aged 50 and above, please advise them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Some people are mixed up over bivalent and the second booster – which all have the concept of two in it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If you use vernacular languages, some of them are even more confusing.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are thinking of some simple publicity, simple graphics, which we intend to use advertising space to communicate and communicate clearly to the public in the next few days.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Should a person who has multiple COVID-19 infections still take the boosters?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Once you reach the booster stage, it is best to ignore your infection.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Now that we have hybrid immunity from our vaccination as well as infection, there are many individuals who hardly have any response or symptoms after they are infected.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I think it is best not to count infections.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Take our boosters and take our jabs diligently.
